title: Korean Traditional Wedding Customs Explained
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
notes: NEW ARTICLE (not a refresh): no old page to read or redirect. SEO checks whether any weddedwonderland.com page already ranks for Korean wedding queries (cannibalisation) and recommends cross-links only.

AUTHORITY RULE (content-system/brand/voice-guide.md 'Write with authority'): no research talk in the copy (what we could or couldn't find, trace or confirm; our sources or method; what the internet says; myths sections; 'you will often read'). Customs without a strong source are written as living practice in a confident voice ('In many Korean families...'), never with a meaning or origin stated as fact. 'Often told' at most once per post, never 'it is often told that'. No hedge stacking: cite a source once by link; date legal and travel facts once per section. Source gaps go in the run report only. No per-line source credits (never 'Britannica describes', 'the museum holds', 'the study records').

Customs vary by family, region and faith, and most Korean couples today hold a Western-style ceremony with a short traditional ceremony (pyebaek) after; say so once. Korean terms in Revised Romanisation as sources give them, with hangeul only where a source gives it.

Likely customs (brief finalises): the traditional ceremony (honrye / jeontong honrye) and its steps; the wooden wedding geese (gireogi, nothing about meaning unless sourced); hanbok for bride and groom (wonsam or hwarot, samogwandae); the pyebaek with the groom's family, jujubes and chestnuts (no meanings as fact unless sourced); the ham (gift box) and its delivery; yedan and yemul exchanges (no amounts); chukuigeum (cash gifts, no amounts); the modern wedding hall format; carrying the bride on the back at the pyebaek as living practice.
UNESCO only where its own text links an element to weddings (e.g. Kimjang 2013, Arirang 2012, if their text names weddings). Confirm each page live and its title.

Destination angle: Smartraveller Republic of Korea checked live (overall level and any higher-level areas, such as near the DMZ, as worded). Legal from official sources only: Australian Embassy Seoul (CNI or affidavit, notarial), Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (recognition), Korean registration (local district office) only if an official page can be read; otherwise questions to ask the district office and the embassy, including any fees; 'as at November 2026'. Seoul and Jeju named only as places couples choose; palaces and hanok villages named only as places, never as venues. Korean-Australian weddings at home.

Sources: Korea Tourism Organization (english.visitkorea.or.kr), the National Folk Museum of Korea, the Academy of Korean Studies / Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, the Korean Cultural Centre Australia, UNESCO, Britannica, the V&A, academic sources. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs or Wikipedia.

Links: Asia destination pages from the link map, related traditions drafts (Japanese, Chinese), /wonderland-concierge, /magazine. UTMs: utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=korean-traditional-wedding&utm_content=primary|secondary.

Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (wooden wedding geese, jujubes and chestnuts) labelled illustrative pending approval; no old page.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches (A: traditional ceremony steps, wedding geese, hanbok, the ham; B: pyebaek, yedan and yemul, chukuigeum, modern wedding hall, UNESCO and legal), 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; self_qa.confidence must be a number; must_include_coverage entries must be objects with covered_by as an array; no extra sourcing rounds; never retry a declined call. Stop at the limit: start no new reads after 15 minutes.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.

Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal or church paperwork.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
